en: Thus have I heard: [The Mahāvaccha Sutta, Discourse to Vaccha, the Seventh in the Majjhima Nikāya]
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Feeding Place.
Then the wanderer Vacchagotta approached the Blessed One and exchanged greetings with him.
When they had concluded their polite and courteous conversation, he sat down to one side. Sitting there, the wanderer Vacchagotta said this to the Blessed One:
“For a long time, Master Gotama, I have been one who shares in conversation with you.
It would be well if Master Gotama would teach me the wholesome and the unwholesome in brief.
“Vaccha, I could teach you the wholesome and the unwholesome in brief, and I could also teach you the wholesome and the unwholesome in detail.”
"Furthermore, Vaccha, I will teach you the wholesome and the unwholesome in brief.
Listen to it and attend closely; I shall speak.
"Yes, sir," the wanderer Vacchagotta replied to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said this:
“Greed, Vaccha, is unwholesome; non-greed is wholesome.
Hatred, Vaccha, is unwholesome; non-hatred is wholesome.”
Delusion, Vaccha, is unwholesome; non-delusion is wholesome.
Thus, Vaccha, these three things are unwholesome, and these three things are wholesome.
Killing living beings, Vaccha, is unwholesome; abstaining from killing living beings is wholesome.
Taking what is not given, Vaccha, is unwholesome; abstaining from taking what is not given is wholesome.
Sexual misconduct, Vaccha, is unwholesome; abstaining from sexual misconduct is wholesome.
False speech, Vaccha, is unwholesome; abstaining from false speech is wholesome.
Slanderous speech, Vaccha, is unwholesome; abstention from slanderous speech is wholesome.
Harsh speech, Vaccha, is unwholesome; abstention from harsh speech is wholesome.
Idle chatter, Vaccha, is unwholesome; abstention from idle chatter is wholesome.
Covetousness, Vaccha, is unwholesome; non-covetousness is wholesome.
Ill will, Vaccha, is unwholesome; non-ill will is wholesome.
Wrong view, Vaccha, is unwholesome; right view is wholesome.
Thus, Vaccha, these ten things are unwholesome, and these ten things are wholesome.
But when, Vaccha, a bhikkhu has abandoned craving— cut it off at the root, made it like a palm stump,

done away with it so that it is no longer subject to future arising— that bhikkhu is an arahant, one whose taints are destroyed, who has lived the holy life, done what was to be done, and laid down the burden.
“Having attained his own goal, with the fetters of existence completely destroyed, he is liberated through right knowledge.
“Let Master Gotama remain for now.

But does Master Gotama have even a single bhikkhu disciple who, by the destruction of the taints, has realized for himself with direct knowledge in this very life the taintless liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom, and having entered upon it, dwells therein?”
“Vaccha, it is not only one hundred, nor two hundred, nor three hundred,
nor four hundred, nor five hundred; indeed, there are even more than that— my bhikkhu disciples who, through the destruction of the taints,
have realized for themselves with direct knowledge in this very life the taintless liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom, and having entered upon them, dwell therein.”
“Let alone Master Gotama; let alone the bhikkhus.

But does Master Gotama have even a single bhikkhunī disciple who, through the destruction of the taints, has realized for herself with direct knowledge in this very life the taintless liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom, and having entered upon it, dwells therein?
“Vaccha, there are not only one hundred, nor two hundred, nor three hundred, nor four hundred...”

“There are five hundred, and indeed more than that, who are my bhikkhunī disciples, who, through the destruction of the taints, have realized for themselves with direct knowledge in this very life the taintless liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom, and dwell having attained them.
“Let alone Master Gotama; let alone the bhikkhus; let alone the bhikkhunīs.”
“But does Master Gotama have even a single lay follower, a disciple clothed in white who lives the holy life, who,
with the total destruction of the five lower fetters, is of spontaneous birth, attaining final Nibbāna there,
not subject to return from that world? “Vaccha, it is not merely one hundred, nor two hundred, nor three hundred, nor four hundred.”

“There are five hundred, and indeed more, lay followers who are my disciples—householders dressed in white, living the holy life—who, through the total destruction of the five lower fetters, are of spontaneous birth, attaining final Nibbāna there, not subject to returning from that world.
“Let it be, Master Gotama; let the bhikkhus stay, let the bhikkhunīs stay, and let the lay followers who are householders dressed in white, living the holy life, stay.”
“But does Master Gotama have even a single lay follower, a disciple who is a householder, dressed in white, enjoying sensual pleasures,
who carries out the teaching, responds to his exhortations, has crossed over doubt, is free from perplexity, has attained self-confidence,
and dwells independent of others in the Teacher’s dispensation?”
“Vaccha, it is not only one hundred, nor two hundred, nor three hundred,
nor four hundred, nor five hundred; rather, there are even more lay followers who are my disciples— householders clad in white, enjoying sensual pleasures,
who act according to my teaching, who respond to my exhortations, who have crossed over doubt, who are free from perplexity, who have attained self-confidence, and who are not dependent on others.”
“...dwelling in the Teacher’s dispensation.

“Let it be, Master Gotama; let the monks stay; let the nuns stay; let the male lay followers, white-robed householders who are celibate, stay; let the male lay followers, white-robed householders who enjoy sensual pleasures, stay.
But does Master Gotama have even a single female lay follower, a disciple, a white-robed householder who is celibate?”
“With the complete destruction of the five lower fetters, she is of spontaneous birth, there attaining final Nibbāna, not subject to return from that world?
“Not just one hundred, Vaccha, nor two hundred, nor three hundred, nor four hundred, nor five hundred;
rather, there are even more than that—female lay disciples of mine, householders dressed in white, living the holy life.”
“With the complete destruction of the five lower fetters, they are of spontaneous birth, attaining final nibbāna there, not subject to return from that world.
“Let Master Gotama remain; let the bhikkhus remain; let the bhikkhunīs remain; let the male lay followers remain.”
"Let alone the white-robed householders who are celibate; let alone the male lay followers (upāsakas) who are white-robed householders enjoying sensual pleasures;
let alone the female lay followers (upāsikās) who are white-robed householders who are celibate.
But does Master Gotama have even a single female lay follower, a disciple who is a white-robed householder enjoying sensual pleasures, yet who carries out the teaching?"
“Is there anyone who, being receptive to instruction, has crossed over doubt, is free from perplexity, has attained self-confidence,
and dwells in the Teacher’s teaching independent of others?
“Not only one hundred, Vaccha, nor two hundred, nor three hundred, nor four hundred, nor— ”
"There are five hundred, and indeed even more than that, female lay disciples of mine— householders dressed in white who enjoy sensual pleasures—
who carry out the teaching, respond to my instructions, have crossed over doubt, are free from perplexity, have attained self-confidence,
and dwell in the Teacher’s dispensation without relying on others."
“For if, Master Gotama, only Master Gotama were one who has attained this Dhamma and the bhikkhus were not attainers of it,
then this holy life would be incomplete in that respect.
But since, Master Gotama, both Master Gotama and the bhikkhus are attainers of this Dhamma, [it is complete].”
In this way, this holy life is complete in that respect.
For if, Master Gotama, you alone were successful in this Dhamma and the bhikkhus were successful, but the bhikkhunīs were not successful,
then this holy life would be incomplete in that respect.
But because, Master Gotama, the Venerable Gotama has mastered this Dhamma, and the bhikkhus have mastered it, and the bhikkhunīs have mastered it—
in this respect, this holy life is complete. For if, Master Gotama,
the Venerable Gotama alone had mastered this Dhamma, and the bhikkhus...
If there were those who had attained success, and if there were nuns who had attained success, but the lay followers—
white-robed householders living the holy life— were not those who had attained success,
then this holy life would be incomplete in that respect.

But because, Master Gotama, the Venerable Gotama has attained this Dhamma, and the bhikkhus have attained it, and the bhikkhunīs have attained it, and the laymen-followers—white-robed householders living the holy life—have attained it;
in this respect, this holy life is complete.
For if, Master Gotama, the Venerable Gotama alone had attained this Dhamma, and the bhikkhus...

The bhikkhus would have been successful, the bhikkhunīs would have been successful, and the laymen householders clad in white who were celibate would have been successful, but the laymen householders clad in white who enjoy sensual pleasures would not have been successful.
In this way, this holy life would have been incomplete in that respect.

But because, Master Gotama, both Master Gotama has accomplished this Dhamma, and the bhikkhus have accomplished it, and the bhikkhunīs have accomplished it, and the laymen followers clothed in white who lead the holy life have accomplished it, and the laymen followers... [have accomplished it].
And laypeople dressed in white, enjoying sensual pleasures, would be successful;
thus this holy life would be fulfilled in that respect.
For if, Master Gotama, you yourself were successful in this Dhamma, and the bhikkhus...

There would have been successful monks, and successful nuns; there would have been successful laymen householders dressed in white who were celibate, and successful laymen householders dressed in white who enjoyed sensual pleasures;
yet there would not have been successful laywomen householders dressed in white who were celibate.
In this way, this holy life would have been incomplete in that respect.

But because, Master Gotama, Master Gotama has accomplished this Dhamma, and the bhikkhus have accomplished it, and the bhikkhunīs have accomplished it, and the laymen householders clothed in white who lead the holy life have accomplished it, and the laymen... [the holy life is complete].
And there are white-robed householders who enjoy sensual pleasures and are successful, as well as white-robed female lay followers who lead the holy life and are successful;
thus this holy life is complete in that respect.
For if, Master Gotama, you yourself were successful in this Dhamma, and the monks...
There would have been successful monks; there would have been successful nuns; there would have been successful laymen householders dressed in white who were celibate;
there would have been successful laymen householders dressed in white who enjoyed sensual pleasures;
and there would have been successful laywomen householders dressed in white who were celibate.
But it would not have been the case that female lay disciples, householders dressed in white who enjoy sensual pleasures, were successful;
thus this holy life would have been incomplete in that respect.
But because, Master Gotama, both Master Gotama himself is successful in this Dhamma and the monks are successful, [it is complete].
The bhikkhunīs were successful; the laymen householders clad in white who were celibate were successful;
the laymen householders clad in white who enjoyed sensual pleasures were successful; the laywomen householders clad in white who were celibate were successful;
and the laywomen householders clad in white who enjoyed sensual pleasures were successful.
"In this way, this holy life is fulfilled in that respect.
Just as, Master Gotama, the river Ganges flows toward the ocean, inclines toward the ocean, tends toward the ocean, and reaches the ocean,
even so this assembly of Master Gotama, consisting of both householders and those gone forth, flows toward Nibbāna."
It inclines toward Nibbāna, leans toward Nibbāna, and stands having reached Nibbāna.
“Excellent, Master Gotama!
… [as before] … I go for refuge to Master Gotama, to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.”
“May I receive the going-forth in the presence of Master Gotama; may I receive the full ordination.
“Vaccha, whoever was formerly a member of another sect who desires the going-forth and desires the full ordination in this Dhamma and Discipline must wait four months as a probationer.
At the end of those four months, if the bhikkhus are satisfied with his mind...”
“They grant the going forth and confer full ordination for the state of a bhikkhu;
nevertheless, I recognize a distinction among individuals in this matter.
“Venerable sir, if those who were formerly members of other sects desire the going forth and desire [full ordination] in this Dhamma and Discipline...”

“They undergo probation for four months regarding full ordination; at the end of those four months, when the monks are pleased, they grant the going-forth and full ordination into the state of a monk. I shall undergo probation for four years.
At the end of those four years, when the monks are pleased, let them grant me the going-forth and full ordination into the state of a monk.”
The wanderer Vacchagotta received the going-forth in the presence of the Blessed One and received full ordination.
Not long after his ordination—having been ordained for half a month—the Venerable Vacchagotta approached the Blessed One;
having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. As the Venerable [Vacchagotta] was sitting there to one side...
Vacchagotta said this to the Blessed One:
“Venerable sir, whatever can be attained by the knowledge of one in training and by the true science of one in training has been attained by me.
May the Blessed One teach me the Dhamma further.”
“In that case, Vaccha, you should further develop two qualities: serenity and insight.
When these two qualities have been further developed by you, Vaccha—serenity and insight—they will lead to the penetration of the various elements.
To whatever extent you may desire:”
‘May I experience the various kinds of psychic power: being one, may I become many; being many, may I become one;
may I appear and disappear; may I pass through walls, fences, and mountains unhindered, as if through space;
and may I dive in and out of the earth, as if it were water.’
‘May I walk on water without sinking, just as on earth; may I travel through the air cross-legged, just like a winged bird;
may I touch and stroke with my hand these very sun and moon, so powerful and majestic;
and may I exercise mastery with my body as far as the Brahma-world.’”
In each and every case, you will attain the capacity for realization whenever there is a suitable basis.
Furthermore, Vaccha, as far as you may wish:

“With the purified divine ear-element, which surpasses the human, may I hear both kinds of sounds—the divine and the human, whether far or near”—in each and every such instance, you will attain the capacity for realization whenever there is a suitable basis.
Therefore, Vaccha, as much as you may wish: ‘May I,
by encompassing with my own mind the minds of other beings, of other persons, understand them—
may I understand a mind affected by lust as a mind affected by lust,’ [you will achieve this].
One should know a mind free from lust as a mind free from lust;
one should know a mind with hatred as a mind with hatred,
or a mind free from hatred as a mind free from hatred.
One should know a mind with delusion as "a mind with delusion," and one should know a mind free from delusion as "a mind free from delusion";
one should know a contracted mind as "a contracted mind."
One should understand a scattered mind as a scattered mind;
one should understand an exalted mind as an exalted mind,
and one should understand a non-exalted mind as a non-exalted mind.
One should understand a surpassable mind as a surpassable mind,
or one should understand an unsurpassable mind as an unsurpassable mind;
or one should understand a concentrated mind as a concentrated mind.
‘May I know an unconcentrated mind as an unconcentrated mind;
may I know a liberated mind as a liberated mind,
and may I know an unliberated mind as an unliberated mind.’”
In each and every case, you will attain the state of being capable of realization, whenever there is an appropriate basis.
Then, Vaccha, as much as you may desire:
"May I recollect my manifold past lives, that is to say, one birth, two births, three births..."
One birth, two births, three births, four births, five births, ten births, twenty births, thirty births,
forty births, fifty births, a hundred births, a thousand births, a hundred thousand births; many aeons of world-contraction,
many aeons of world-expansion, many aeons of both world-contraction and expansion— "I existed there..."
"Such was my name, such my clan, such my appearance, such my food, such my experience of pleasure and pain, and such the limit of my lifespan;
passing away from there, I arose elsewhere. There too I had such a name, such a clan, such an appearance, such food, such an experience of pleasure and pain, and such a limit of lifespan;
passing away from there, I reappeared here"—thus he recollects his manifold past lives in their modes and details.
‘May I recollect my past lives,’ in each such case you will attain the capacity for realization, provided there is a suitable basis.
Therefore, Vaccha, as far as you may desire:
‘With the divine eye, purified and surpassing that of humans, may I see beings passing away and being reborn—
inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate— and may I understand how beings fare according to their kamma, thinking: “Alas, these worthy beings,
possessed of misconduct of body, possessed of misconduct of speech, and possessed of misconduct of mind...”’
Those noble ones who were possessed of [evil conduct], revilers of the noble ones, holding wrong views, and undertaking actions based on wrong views,
at the breaking up of the body, after death, have been reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, even in hell;
whereas these worthy beings, however, were possessed of good conduct of body, possessed of good conduct of speech, and possessed of good conduct of mind.
“Those who do not revile the noble ones, who hold right view, and who undertake actions based on right view— on the dissolution of the body, after death, they are reborn in a happy destination,
a heavenly world. Thus, with the divine eye, purified and surpassing that of humans,
one might see beings passing away and being reborn— lowly and exalted, beautiful and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate.
‘May I know beings as they pass away according to their karma’—
in each such case, you will attain the capacity for realization, provided there is a suitable basis.
Therefore, Vaccha, as far as you may desire:
‘May I, through the destruction of the taints, dwell in this very life having realized for myself with direct knowledge the taintless liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom,
and having entered upon it’— in each such case, you will attain the capacity to be a witness,

provided there is a suitable basis. Then the Venerable Vacchagotta, having delighted and rejoiced in the Blessed One’s words, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, and keeping him to his right, departed.
Then, dwelling alone, withdrawn, diligent, ardent, and resolute, the Venerable Vacchagotta, in no long time,

realized for himself through direct knowledge, in this very life, that supreme goal of the holy life, for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness; and having attained it, he dwelt therein.
“Birth is exhausted, the holy life has been lived, what was to be done has been done, there is nothing further of this state of being”—thus he directly knew.
And so the venerable Vacchagotta became one of the arahants.
Now at that time, a number of bhikkhus were going to see the Blessed One.
The Venerable Vacchagotta saw those bhikkhus coming from afar.
Having seen them, he approached those bhikkhus and, having approached, said this to them:
"Well now, venerable sirs, where are you going?"
“Friends, let us go to see the Blessed One.
“In that case, venerable ones, pay homage with your heads at the feet of the Blessed One in my name, and say this:
‘Venerable sir, the bhikkhu Vacchagotta pays homage with his head at the feet of the Blessed One, and he says this:’”
“The Blessed One has been served by me; the Sugata has been served by me.
“So it is, friend,” those bhikkhus replied to the Venerable Vacchagotta.
Then those bhikkhus approached the Blessed One; having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, they sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, those bhikkhus said this to the Blessed One:
“Venerable sir, the Venerable Vacchagotta pays homage with his head at the Blessed One’s feet and says this:
‘The Blessed One has been served by me; the Sugata has been served by me.
“Bhikkhus, I had already known the bhikkhu Vacchagotta by encompassing his mind with my own mind:”
“The bhikkhu Vacchagotta is a possessor of the threefold knowledge, one of great psychic power and great majesty.
Even deities have informed me of this matter:
“Venerable sir, the bhikkhu Vacchagotta is a possessor of the threefold knowledge, one of great psychic power and great majesty.”
Thus spoke the Blessed One.
Delighted, those bhikkhus rejoiced in the words of the Blessed One.
The Mahāvaccha Sutta, the third, is finished.
